title: 2017 AMC 10A Problem 17
statement:
Distinct points \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(R,\) \(S\) lie on the circle \(x^{2}+y^{2}=25\) and have integer coordinates. The distances \(PQ\) and \(RS\) are irrational numbers.

What is the greatest possible value of the ratio \(\dfrac{PQ}{RS}?\)

solutions.text:
The integer-coordinate points on \(x^2+y^2=25\) are \((\pm5,0)\), \((0,\pm5)\), \((\pm3,\pm4)\), and \((\pm4,\pm3)\).

For \(PQ\) and \(RS\) to be irrational, the squared distance must not be a perfect square. To maximize the ratio, make \(PQ\) as large as possible and \(RS\) as small as possible under that condition.

The largest possible irrational distance is between \((-4,3)\) and \((3,-4)\), giving \(PQ=\sqrt{7^2+7^2}=\sqrt{98}\). The smallest possible irrational distance is between \((3,4)\) and \((4,3)\), giving \(RS=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt2\).

The greatest possible ratio is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{98}}{\sqrt2}=7\). Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: List the lattice points on the circle
